subject: Hosted qualification playbook + workshop invite

Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo notes — clarification on Hosted vs Dedicated vs VPC

Hi Ava + Claire,

Thanks for taking the demo earlier — really helpful to see ClearCart's summarization flow and the latency expectations you mentioned. Quick recap + ask so we can follow up with a narrow technical workshop: 

What we heard from the call:
- Primary use case: extractive + abstractive summarization for order confirmation emails and chat transcripts.
- Expected peak: ~200 RPS during daily spikes (~3 hours), baseline ~40 RPS.
- Target latency: 95th < 200ms for the short-summary endpoint.
- Quality and audit: you need log-level auditability and SOC2 evidence; VPC/air-gapped is not required today but may be requested by your security team later.
- Data residency: US-only preferred.

Immediate qualification question: given the traffic and the desire to iterate quickly, Hosted API looks like the fastest path to evaluate (sandbox endpoints + rate slice). Dedicated or Private VPC would make sense if you need sustained throughput at predictable cost or strict network isolation.

Proposed next steps: 
1) Quick technical workshop (30–45m) this week to map endpoints and expected payloads.
2) We’ll spin up a Hosted sandbox with 2 endpoints ("short-summary" and "embeddings") and a conservative rate window for you to smoke test.
3) Share a short Hosted Quickstart checklist + sample config for your engineering team.

Can you confirm: preferred time for workshop (Thu or Fri mornings PT) and whether you want us to include a short cost/throughput snapshot vs Dedicated capacity?

Attachments: demo-recording.mp4 (we captured the session)

Thanks —
Sergio Alvarez

Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 17:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo notes — clarification on Hosted vs Dedicated vs VPC

Thanks, Sergio — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Traffic: that 200 RPS is a peak estimate for a promotional window; sustained daily average is closer to 60–80 RPS. Total daily token volume is roughly 600k–900k tokens depending on prompt size.
- SLA: our product team wants < 250ms P95 for UI-facing calls.
- Security: SOC2 is sufficient for now. VPC/private would be a ‘nice to have’ later if we move PII-heavy flows on-prem.
- Cost sensitivity: we’re evaluating unit cost — would love a simple Hosted vs Dedicated delta for a 6–12 month pilot.

Workshop: Friday 10:00 AM PT works for Claire and me. Please invite and include an ops-focused engineer if possible.

Two asks for the sandbox:
1) Can you set an initial rate window that allows burst testing up to 300 RPS for short periods?
2) Any guidance on prefix/KV caching — we expect a lot of repeated templates.

Appreciate it — looking forward to the checklist.

— Ava
Head of Product, ClearCart
ava@clearcart.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, chloe_martin@redwood.com
Cc: Ava Park <ava@clearcart.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Hosted sandbox recommendation + initial ratecap plan

Sergio / Chloe — following up with a short technical recommendation to bring to Friday’s workshop. Leaving the business notes in Sergio's thread so Ava has context.

Recommendation (Hosted sandbox, initial config):
- Endpoints to provision: /v1/short-summary (generation), /v1/embeddings (embedding-only).
- Sandbox rate windows: base 100 RPS per endpoint, burst up to 300 RPS for 10m windows (use burst quota for stress tests).
- Concurrency guidance: limit concurrent streams to 50 per endpoint to keep p95 < 250ms; enable streaming for the UI route.
- Token budgeting: plan for ~350 tokens per short-summary request (prompt + completion budget); set token-limit guard rails in the sandbox to avoid surprises.
- Caching: enable prefix/KV caching for the short-summary endpoint for template-heavy traffic — this should reduce token consumption on repeated prompts by ~30–40% in typical runs.
- Fallbacks: configure automatic fallback to a cheaper model variant (quantized) for non-critical background summarization.

When to recommend Dedicated or Private VPC:
- Strong candidate for Dedicated if: sustained throughput > 5k tokens/sec or predictable burst budgets are central to your SLOs and you want committed unit pricing.
- Private VPC recommended if: legal/regulatory restrictions require customer-controlled networking or HSM-based key management.

Attachments: hosted-quickstart-checklist.pdf, sample-config.yaml

I’ll prepare a 15-minute ops slide for Friday with these items and a short risk checklist (network egress, token spikes, monitoring hooks).

-Neha
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
